heroSubtitle: An experienced newborn caretaker so the baby's bath, feeds and sleep have a rhythm — and you get the rest recovery actually needs. Message us your delivery month and area; the good caretakers get reserved early.
whoIsItFor: Your delivery is next month and no one from family can fly in for the first six weeks.
You're recovering from a C-section and being awake all night with the baby is setting you back.
It's your first baby, and you want someone who has done this a hundred times, right beside you.

availableWorkers: The caretakers you'll meet have handled newborns before — holding the head, burping after feeds, bath temperature, the endless 2am wake-ups. They work under your guidance, not over it: you remain the parent making every call. You see each profile and speak with them before day one.

unaskedQAs.question: How early should we start looking?
unaskedQAs.answer: Two to four weeks before your due month. The experienced newborn caretakers get reserved — a March baby and a December baby don't have the same availability.

unaskedQAs.question: Will she wake us for every feed?
unaskedQAs.answer: Agree the night split before she starts. Live-in caretakers take the scheduled night feeds and diaper changes so you sleep in real stretches; you're woken for what only you can do.

unaskedQAs.question: My mother-in-law will be here for a month — is that a problem?
unaskedQAs.answer: It usually helps. Tell us in the first message if another senior family member will be present; duties get arranged around who does what.

unaskedQAs.question: Does she do the mother's massage too?
unaskedQAs.answer: Many do, as an extra agreed between your family and her — with oils you choose. Ask during the introduction; it's never assumed.

unaskedQAs.question: What if the baby gets a fever at night?
unaskedQAs.answer: She is not a nurse and cannot treat illness — she'll bring it to you immediately and stay up with the baby while you call your pediatrician. Keep your pediatrician's night number saved before day one.

unaskedQAs.question: Can she handle twins?
unaskedQAs.answer: Say so in the first message. Twin experience is specific — some caretakers have it, many don't, and you'll only see profiles where it's stated.

unaskedQAs.question: What do you need from us in the first message?
unaskedQAs.answer: Your area, the due month or the baby's age, day shift or live-in, and anything unusual we should know. That's enough to check availability today.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a newborn care worker and a general babysitter?
faqs.answer: A newborn caretaker specialises in the first year: head-support handling, cord-area care, sterilisation of bottles and pumps, soothing techniques. A general babysitter is for older babies and toddlers — a different skill and different instincts.

faqs.question: Can we hire a live-in newborn caretaker for 24 hours?
faqs.answer: Yes — live-in arrangements include nights, with structured rest hours for her too. It's not 24 hours of continuous wakefulness; the night duties are split and agreed before she starts.

faqs.question: Do the caretakers help with washing baby clothes and bottles?
faqs.answer: Yes — baby clothes and linens are washed separately, and bottles, pumps and accessories are washed and sterilised after every feed.

faqs.question: How do you select your newborn care personnel?
faqs.answer: Experience with infants, patience under sleepless conditions, hygienic habits and references from previous families are all checked before a profile reaches you. You still meet the person before deciding.

faqs.question: Can the caretaker provide traditional baby massage in Chennai style?
faqs.answer: Yes — most are experienced in the traditional style, using only the oils your family or pediatrician approves. Say your preference during the introduction.

faqs.question: How far in advance should we book newborn care in Chennai?
faqs.answer: Two to four weeks before the due date. Tell us the month in your first WhatsApp message and we'll check which caretakers are actually free then — not just today.
